title: Worktree add failure leaves 'out' undefined and crashes the script in finally/parse flow

finding.claim: Worktree add failure leaves 'out' undefined and crashes the script in finally/parse flow
finding.evidence: The subprocess that creates the worktree is checked and can raise before 'out' is assigned, but the code later iterates 'out.splitlines()' unconditionally.
finding.recommendation: Initialize 'out' before the try block and return a controlled failure report when worktree creation or test execution fails. Also guard the parsing loop so it only runs when command output was actually captured.

code_region.text:
def main():
    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="pt1-hardening-pf-")
    wt = os.path.join(tmp, "wt")
    lines = ["HARDENING PARENT-FAIL VERIFICATION",
             f"Test file from HEAD overlaid on parent {PARENT} "
             "(pre-hardening).", ""]
    try:
        subprocess.run(["git", "worktree", "add", "--detach",
                        wt, PARENT], cwd=REPO, check=True,
                       capture_output=True, text=True)
        shutil.copy(os.path.join(
            REPO, "tests", "test_v111_hardening.py"),
            os.path.join(wt, "tests", "test_v111_hardening.py"))
        proc = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-m", "unittest", "-v",
             "tests.test_v111_hardening"],
            cwd=wt, capture_output=True, text=True)
        out = proc.stdout + proc.stderr
    finally:
        subprocess.run(["git", "worktree", "remove", "--force",
                        wt], cwd=REPO, capture_output=True)

refutation.reason: The code initializes 'out' via proc.stdout and proc.stderr before the finally block, and the finally block only removes the worktree; the subsequent loop iterates over 'out' which is always assigned when the loop executes because it is defined in the try block before the finally clause.

probe.summary: Probe-scripts probe (`probes/closing_probe_scripts_probe.py`, section b): the subject (the committed hardening_parent_fail probe) was executed with its git worktree-add forced to fail (bad revision). Exit code 1; the traceback is a CalledProcessError out of subprocess.run — NameError/UnboundLocalError present in the traceback: False. The claimed mechanism (a NameError from parsing an unbound 'out' after a swallowed failure) does NOT occur: the exception propagates through the finally and the parse loop is never reached. What IS true: the failure surfaces as an uncontrolled traceback rather than a controlled failure report — the substance of the claim (no error handling at this site) survives at probe-tooling severity.
